title: Confronting Atheism and Contemporary Doubts
summary: As your son stands on the threshold of university and the open world, he will encounter organized doubts: atheism, skepticism about the religion, and mockery of its constants online. Your role is not to prevent him from hearing these things, but to fortify him. Teach him that a doubt (shubhah) is a question with an answer, and that many who cast doubts do so from ignorance or desire. Train him to seek answers from trusted scholars of knowledge rather than accepting anything from anyone. Help him distinguish between a question that seeks the truth and a doubt that seeks destruction. The most important thing you can give him is confidence that his religion stands firm in the face of debate, and that he is not alone.
try_this: This week: Discuss a common doubt your son sees online calmly, and search together for a reliable scholarly response—teach him *how to think*, not just *what to answer*.
reflection_prompts: How can you fortify your son against doubts without isolating him from the world?
What is the difference between a question that seeks the truth and a doubt that seeks destruction, and how can your son distinguish between them?
